text:
marie: Heads up — saw a spike of NAT_BACKEND_503 alerts last night around 03:10-03:40. Looks like a recurring pulse over the last 3 days, same source service (edge-proxy-prod). Posting quick screenshots and counts in case useful.
aj: Which service exactly? any correlating deploy or scheduled job?
marie: edge-proxy-prod. No deploys in that window per deploy-bot. The pulses are ~30m apart, affecting 5-10% of requests during bursts. Chart: <link>.
sam: Can we group/dedupe by request path + downstream-id? Feels like the same source flapping.
leo: We already fingerprint some 5xxs, but this is an aggregated backend 503 that pages P0. Might be better to move to a rate-based alert (5m window) and group by path + backend name.
tess: Agree we shouldn't mask real incidents. Proposed short plan: 1) quick threshold adjustment to reduce paging for known noise, 2) add a dedupe/grouping rule to alertmanager, 3) long-term root-cause and postmortem if noise persists.
aj: I can own the quick change to the alert expression (rate-window + adjusted threshold) and roll to prod today. I'll open a ticket and run it in staging first.
ops-bot: New ticket created: INF-2489 - tune NAT_BACKEND_503 alert — assigned to @aj, due in 3 days.
marie: For long-term: we need remediation ownership (who will implement dedupe), timelines, and a small follow-up doc that we can reference in future postmortems.
sam: I'll take the dedupe implementation (alertmanager grouping + prometheus relabeling). ETA 14 days. I'll propose a fingerprint that uses request_path + backend_id. Example rule I plan to start from:
```
- alert: HighNATBackend5xx
  expr: increase(http_requests_total{job=\"edge-proxy\",status=~\"5..\"}[5m]) / increase(http_requests_total{job=\"edge-proxy\"}[5m]) > 0.02
  for: 10m
  labels: {severity: \"warning\"}
```
This should be less reactive than the instantaneous spike.
leo: I'll own the follow-up doc + weekly incident digest entry so we have the pattern tracked. ETA 4 days.
tess: Also suggest a paging policy tweak: don't page overnight for this alert unless error rate is >5% AND latency is elevated. Can someone put a proposal into the paging policy repo? @eng-sre
aj: Quick change is ready — PR opened for threshold -> 0.5% over baseline for 5m and adjusted for: 10m. Will test in staging then merge.
marie: Please include a clear rollback plan in the PR description and link to runbook: /runbook/prod/alerts/nat_503. If it causes regressions we need to revert fast.
sam: PR for dedupe config coming next week, will include tests on the staging alertmanager instance.
ops-bot: INF-2489 updated: threshold change + alert text + temp suppression window added. Status: in progress.
deploy-bot: Deployment started: edge-proxy-prod v2.31 by @aj.
marie: Early signal shows reduced pages at 04:15. I'll keep monitoring overnight and will update INF-2489 tomorrow. If stable, we'll close the quick-fix and keep dedupe task for later.
aj: INF-2489 updated with test notes and production rollout timestamp. Leaving dedupe to @sam as planned.
leo: Added digest note: "nat-backend-noise: initial reduction after threshold tuning; dedupe pending" to the weekly ops digest.
tess: Recap of action items: INF-2489 (aj) quick threshold change, due in 3d; INF-2520 (sam) dedupe + fingerprinting, due in 14d; DOC-77 (leo) incident digest + follow-up doc, due in 4d. Assign reviewers: eng-infra.
marie: Thanks all. Let's reconvene in the weekly alerts sync to validate the dedupe plan and check for any collateral misses. If anyone spots an unintended suppression ping me directly. :bow:
